name: MathlibAnnex.Analysis.CStarAlgebra.NonUnitalCStarRepresentation.countable_characterSpace_of_nonUnital_singleton
title: The full character space is countable

content.display_title: The full character space is countable
content.one_sentence_role: Uses separated unit eigenvectors to count the non-scalar characters, then restores the one scalar character.
content.natural_language_statement: Let $A$ be a nonzero complex $C^*$-algebra, with no unit assumed. Let $H$ be a separable complex Hilbert space, and let $\pi:A\to\mathcal B(H)$ be nonzero irreducible and represent the unique unitary-equivalence class of nonzero irreducible comparisons. If $D$ is a norm-closed unital $*$-subalgebra of $\widetilde A=\mathbb C\oplus A$, then the entire character space $X$ of $D$ is countable. Here $\chi_\infty(\lambda,a)=\lambda$ denotes the scalar-coordinate character of $\widetilde A$.
content.assumptions: Commutativity of $D$ is not an additional hypothesis in this theorem. Separability is imposed on $H$, not on $A$ or $D$.
content.conclusion: Countability includes the scalar character $\chi_\infty|_D$, as well as all the other characters.
content.proof_summary: Choose a unit eigenvector for each non-scalar character, prove their pairwise orthogonality, count disjoint small balls using separability, and adjoin the scalar character.
proof_steps: Let $Y=X\setminus\{\chi_\infty|_D\}$. For each $\chi\in Y$, apply [A joint unit eigenvector for each non-scalar character](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/NonUnital/CharacterEigenvector.lean#L85-L197) with the same $A,H,\pi,D$ and that $\chi$. Closedness of $D$ and its inequality from the scalar character supply the remaining hypotheses. Fix a unit vector $\eta_\chi$ for each character so that $$\widehat\pi(d)\eta_\chi=\chi(d)\eta_\chi\qquad(d\in D),$$ where $\widehat\pi(\lambda,a)=\lambda I+\pi(a)$.

If $\chi\ne\psi$, choose $d\in D$ with $\chi(d)\ne\psi(d)$. Put $T=\widehat\pi(d)$. Since $D$ is $*$-closed, the eigenvector equation also gives $T^*\eta_\psi=\overline{\psi(d)}\eta_\psi$. With the inner product linear in its second argument, $$\overline{\psi(d)}\langle\eta_\chi,\eta_\psi\rangle=\langle\eta_\chi,T^*\eta_\psi\rangle=\langle T\eta_\chi,\eta_\psi\rangle=\overline{\chi(d)}\langle\eta_\chi,\eta_\psi\rangle.$$ The two coefficients differ, so $\langle\eta_\chi,\eta_\psi\rangle=0$.

Consequently $$\|\eta_\chi-\eta_\psi\|^2=\|\eta_\chi\|^2+\|\eta_\psi\|^2=2.$$ The open balls $B(\eta_\chi,1/3)$ are therefore nonempty and pairwise disjoint. Choose a countable dense set in $H$; each ball contains a point of it, and disjoint balls require different points. Thus $Y$ is countable. This is the separated-ball argument in [Countability of the non-scalar character space](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/NonUnital/CharacterCountable.lean#L38-L93).
Finally $$X=Y\cup\{\chi_\infty|_D\}.$$ Adding this one character to the countable set $Y$ proves countability of the entire character space.
